info.name: AWARDS FHIR® API Documentation
info.description:
This document is for use by Health IT developers seeking to use our ONC Certified (g)(10) Standardized API for Health Level 7 (HL7®) Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR®) services.

Base URL: https://fhir.footholdtechnology.com/{provider}
Service Base URL List: https://fhir.footholdtechnology.com/Endpoint

Configuration Requirements:

  1. Must support TLS 1.2 and above

  2. Must support OAuth 2.0 authorization

  3. Must be able to read and parse JSON responses

  4. Must follow "App protection" rules as outlined in the specification http://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/#app-protection

Standards Supported:

  • Bulk Data Access (Flat FHIR) STU
    HL7 FHIR® Bulk Data Access (Flat FHIR®) (v1.0.0: STU 1), August 22, 2019

  • HL7 FHIR Specification
    HL7 Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources Specification (FHIR®) Release 4, Version 4.0.1: R4, October 30, 2019, including Technical Correction #1, November 1, 2019

  • SMART Application Launch Framework IG
    HL7 FHIR® SMART Application Launch Framework Implementation Guide Release 1.0.0, November 13, 2018

  • US Core IG
    HL7 FHIR® US Core Implementation Guide STU 6.1.0, June 19, 2023

  • USCDI (United States Core Data for Interoperability)
    United States Core Data for Interoperability (USCDI), Version 3, October 2022 Errata

App Registration:
Developers wishing to integrate must contact the respective provider directly. Foothold Technology will reach out once the respective provider approves access. Each Provider is considered a separate entity and will have its own API URL and registration. Each Provider is responsible for maintaining the rights of their API accounts.

item.name: Authentication

exec: // Add the token to the collection variables

request.description:
Token Generation

This endpoint allows you to generate a token by making an HTTP POST request. The returned token is required to retrieve FHIR resources.

Request Body

  • audience (text): The type of audience for the token.

  • grant_type (text): The type of grant for the token.

  • client_id (text): The client ID for authentication.

  • client_secret (text): The client secret for authentication.

Response

Upon successful execution, the server responds with a status code of 200 and a JSON object containing the following fields:

  • access_token: The generated access token.

  • scope: The scope of the token.

  • expires_in: The expiration time of the token.

  • token_type: The type of the token.

Token Information Endpoint

This endpoint allows you to retrieve information about a token.

Request Body

The request should be sent as x-www-form-urlencoded with the following parameter:

  • token (text): The token for which you want to retrieve information.

Response

The response will include the details of the token, such as its type, expiration, and any associated user information.

item.description:
This folder contains essential requests for obtaining and managing access tokens required to interact with the FHIR API endpoints.

Token Request - API:

This request is used to generate a token which is necessary to call any further FHIR resources.

Note: When making a request to receive a token, the Content-Type must be of application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

Token Instrospection:

This request will return information about the token and it's payload.

Token Revoke:

This request will ensures that the users Access and Refresh Tokens cannot be reused

item.description:
A reference to a document of any kind for any purpose. Provides metadata about the document so that the document can be discovered and managed. The scope of a document is any seralized object with a mime-type, so includes formal patient centric documents (CDA), cliical notes, scanned paper, and non-patient specific documents like policy text.

The following profiles are supported:

  • US Core DocumentReference Profile

US Core Data Element:

US Core Data Element FHIR Resource Data
Consultation Note DocumentReference.type = "11488-4"
Discharge Summary DocumentReference.type = "18842-5"
History & Physical Note DocumentReference.type = "34117-2"
Procedures Note DocumentReference.type = "28570-0"
Progress Note DocumentReference.type = "11506-3"

item.description:
Provenance of a resource is a record that describes entities and processes involved in producing and delivering or otherwise influencing that resource. Provenance provides a critical foundation for assessing authenticity, enabling trust, and allowing reproducibility. Provenance assertions are a form of contextual metadata and can themselves become important records with their own provenance. Provenance statement indicates clinical significance in terms of confidence in authenticity, reliability, and trustworthiness, integrity, and stage in lifecycle (e.g. Document Completion - has the artifact been legally authenticated), all of which may impact security, privacy, and trust policies.

The following profiles are supported:

  • US Core Provenance Profile
US Core Data Element FHIR Resource Data
Author Time Stamp Provenance.recorded

This folder contains endpoints for accessing various FHIR resources. Each subfolder focuses on a specific resource type, providing detailed requests to retrieve healthcare data according to the FHIR specification.

Usage:

Each subfolder within "FHIR Resources" includes detailed endpoints for interacting with the respective FHIR resource. These endpoints are designed to comply with the FHIR specification, ensuring compatibility and interoperability with other FHIR-compliant systems.
